engineering-presentation-css-scopedengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0.625 of 0.625 (major)passThe sample presentation owns one stylesheet, how-to.css, which Talk.tsx imports. Talk.tsx wraps the deck in the root class `how-to`. Every rule in how-to.css that targets a kit hook or a generic element sits under `.how-to`. That covers the root, header, title, marker, mode toggle, prev/next buttons, footer, caption, dots, the `[data-presentation-attribution]` hook, the TOC entries, and every rule inside the @media (max-width: 640px) block. Kit hooks used inside the scene are scoped under `.how-to-scene`, the class the presentation puts on its own SceneLayer. Every other selector (.how-to-actor, .how-to-card[data-kind=&#39;ghost&#39;], .how-to-arrow path, .how-to-frame-label and so on) is a class namespaced to this presentation. Those classes are its own hooks: only this presentation applies them, in SampleScene.tsx, so the rules cannot match elements in another presentation after client-side navigation. The materialized template presentation.css follows the same pattern. Its kit-hook rules sit under `.__CLASS__`, its other selectors are `.__CLASS__-box` and `.__CLASS__-arrow`, and new-presentation.mjs replaces `__CLASS__` with the slug. Judge C failed the criterion because .how-to-actor, .how-to-card[data-kind=&#39;ghost&#39;] and .how-to-arrow path have no `.how-to` ancestor. That reason does not decide the requirement. The requirement allows scoping under the presentation&#39;s own root class or hook, and these selectors target the presentation&#39;s own namespaced hook classes, which it alone renders. They are not unscoped rules that could leak to other presentations, which is the defect the criterion names. Judges A and B are borne out by the material, so I rule pass.how-to.css lines 2-139: the root rule `.how-to` and every kit-hook and button rule are prefixed `.how-to `, including line 106 `.how-to [data-presentation-attribution]` | how-to.css lines 255-287: every rule inside the @media block is prefixed `.how-to ` | how-to.css lines 142-252: kit hooks in the scene are under `.how-to-scene` (lines 145-146); the other selectors are presentation-namespaced classes (.how-to-actor, .how-to-card, .how-to-arrow, ...) | Talk.tsx line 3 imports ./how-to.css and line 9 renders &lt;div className=&quot;how-to&quot;&gt; as the presentation root | templates/presentation/presentation.css: kit-hook selectors are under `.__CLASS__` (lines 24-57) and the others are `.__CLASS__-box` and `.__CLASS__-arrow`; new-presentation.mjs line 37 replaces __CL… | quoted lines: src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/how-to.css:1-140 | quoted lines: src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/how-to.css:141-287 | quoted lines: src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx:1-13 | quoted lines: skills/presentation/templates/presentation/presentation.css:1-58 | quoted lines: skills/presentation/scripts/new-presentation.mjs:37-37 | decider ruling: pass, confirmed by the closed-world span audit | judging basis: decider-pass | src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/how-to.css | src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx | skills/presentation/templates/presentation/presentation.css | skills/presentation/scripts/new-presentation.mjs

Every step therefore gets the same key, and the same SampleScene instance stays mounted and only receives a new payload. It is not remounted or cross-faded. Identity: the presentation owns the entity namespace in entities.ts (`ENTITY_IDS`, `EntityId`, `APPEARS_AT`, `RECTS`, `LINKS`). SampleScene.tsx&#39;s `RENDER: Record&lt;EntityId, ...&gt;` has one entry per id. It passes each id as the `id` prop of the rendered node: Box (you, prompt, skill, tray, socket, verify, and card1-3 and ghost via StepCard), Arrow (convoArrow, link12, link23, linkVerify, modifyArc), SymbolChip (questionChip, chip12, chip23, modifyChip, control, passChip via Chip), Emphasis (flag), Frame (frame), and Label (frameLabel). `entitiesAt(payload.step)` maps over these ids, wrapping each in `&lt;Appear key={id}&gt;`, so a persisting entity keeps the same React key and the same id from step to step. Every node consumer forwards the id as `layoutId`. Box, Label, SymbolChip, Emphasis and Frame spread `morphProps(id)` from nodes/props.ts, which sets `layout: true`, `layoutId: id` and a layout transition. Arrow sets `layoutId={id}` directly on its `motion.svg`. Appear and SceneLayer carry no entity identity. They only add the fade wrapper and the layer, and the Appear key is the entity id. Stage wraps the scene in `LayoutGroup`. Navigating between adjacent steps therefore keeps the SampleScene instance and animates each entity with the same layoutId in place. This applies to all 24 ids in `ENTITY_IDS`, each of which is consumed by a rendered node. groupKey preserves the scene mount, and the ENTITY ids carried through layoutId preserve entity identity. Box, Label, SymbolChip, Emphasis and Frame spread `morphProps(id)`, which sets `layout: true` and `layoutId: id`. Arrow sets `layoutId={id}` on `motion.svg`. Stage wraps the scene in `LayoutGroup`. Appear does not set a layoutId, and its `id` prop goes unused. No ENTITY member is left unconsumed, and the rationale keeps groupKey (scene mount) separate from layoutId (entity identity). SceneLayer and the kit&#39;s index.ts re-export are not in the packet. The verifier then waits 10 s and fails as &#39;VERIFY FAIL [render] ... first step did not render (no [data-step-count] hook)&#39; (scripts/verify.mjs:89-97). That is a render-phase timeout, not a sample check reporting the sample missing. Judge B&#39;s reason is borne out and decides the requirement. Judges A and C cite the registry-removal and out-of-order e2e faults (tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts:62-75). Root cause: `word` is built from single characters, so the keyword check never matches. End-to-end: a valid registry with such a function above the array fails verify with `[sample] … not registered`. Prediction was wrong, which is the finding: F-3 remains."},{"line":2311,"text":""},{"line":2312,"text":"**X2 Regex-versus-division decisions.** Predicted: division keeps the following comment and string state intact. Test setup. The integration and end-to-end suites may assume Chromium is already available, from a cache or a prior install. The test plan lists that as setup. This repository's own `npm run verify` may also rely on the `README.md` instruction (`npx playwright install chromium`), because the repository has no hosted CI."},{"line":2638,"text":" 2. The shipped skill. The `README.md` is not part of `skills/presentation/` or the bootstrap, so it cannot serve a generated app. The Playwright npm package is installed by `scaffold.mjs --apply`, but the browser binary is a separate download. A freshly scaffolded app on a machine without Chromium would otherwise fail with a raw launch error. That breaks \"does not assume dependencies are installed\" and the self-verify gate. The skill must therefore carry an explicit step, in the distributable files, that ensures Chromium before the first render check. The design places this in \"the verify step\", and `SKILL.md` section 4 (Self-verify) qualifies, as does the scaffold apply step. A suitable form is running `npx playwright install chromium` inside the app directory, which does nothing when the browser is already present. A launch failure in the verify and inspect scripts should also stop with an actionable message that names that command and the failed phase, never a silent skip and never reported as a pass."},{"line":2639,"text":""},{"line":2640,"text":" Today `SKILL.md` has no such step and the bootstrap carries no setup note, so this is a gap in the distributable skill. It needs a documentation or procedure fix and does not need a new test. The existing test setup and the INT-001 and E2E-001 passes are unaffected."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0d38817e8afb33fc (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":3836,"end_line":3837,"lines":[{"line":3836,"text":"## Cross-group cross-fade with a shared layout id"},{"line":3837,"text":"Choice: kept `AnimatePresence` in default sync mode with `LayoutGroup`; verified in a real browser that the outgoing scene unmounts after a cross-group transition sharing an entity id (jsdom cannot show this, so the unit test uses distinct ids). Rationale: the environment's preinstalled Chromium (`/ms-playwright/chromium-1228`) matches 1.61.x; the latest release wants a browser that is not installed and cannot be launched offline. If wrong: on a machine with a different browser build run `npx playwright install chromium` or bump the pin together in both manifests and the bootstrap lockfile. End-to-end: a valid registry with such a function above the array fails verify with `[sample] … not registered`. Test setup. The integration and end-to-end suites may assume Chromium is already available, from a cache or a prior install. The test plan lists that as setup. This repository's own `npm run verify` may also rely on the `README.md` instruction (`npx playwright install chromium`), because the repository has no hosted CI."},{"line":2638,"text":" 2. The shipped skill. The `README.md` is not part of `skills/presentation/` or the bootstrap, so it cannot serve a generated app. The Playwright npm package is installed by `scaffold.mjs --apply`, but the browser binary is a separate download. A freshly scaffolded app on a machine without Chromium would otherwise fail with a raw launch error. That breaks \"does not assume dependencies are installed\" and the self-verify gate. The skill must therefore carry an explicit step, in the distributable files, that ensures Chromium before the first render check. The design places this in \"the verify step\", and `SKILL.md` section 4 (Self-verify) qualifies, as does the scaffold apply step. A suitable form is running `npx playwright install chromium` inside the app directory, which does nothing when the browser is already present. A launch failure in the verify and inspect scripts should also stop with an actionable message that names that command and the failed phase, never a silent skip and never reported as a pass."},{"line":2639,"text":""},{"line":2640,"text":" Today `SKILL.md` has no such step and the bootstrap carries no setup note, so this is a gap in the distributable skill. It needs a documentation or procedure fix and does not need a new test. The existing test setup and the INT-001 and E2E-001 passes are unaffected."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0d38817e8afb33fc (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":3836,"end_line":3837,"lines":[{"line":3836,"text":"## Cross-group cross-fade with a shared layout id"},{"line":3837,"text":"Choice: kept `AnimatePresence` in default sync mode with `LayoutGroup`; verified in a real browser that the outgoing scene unmounts after a cross-group transition sharing an entity id (jsdom cannot show this, so the unit test uses distinct ids). In all four copies (repository and bootstrap, verify and inspect), every one of those paths reaches a finally block that calls `await preview.stop()`. That `stop()` sends SIGTERM to the `node vite.js preview` child process it spawned directly, escalates to SIGKILL after 3 s, and waits for the exit. It is not killing an npm or npx wrapper. If the browser fails to launch, `browser` is still undefined, so `browser?.close()` does nothing and `stop()` runs. If a check or step fails, the error passes through the same finally.
